title: Remove the Rogue Package
description: A novelty package 'sl' was installed on a staging box; remove and purge it completely.
scenario: The quarterly software audit found the novelty package 'sl' (the steam locomotive) installed on this staging server. Policy says unapproved packages must be removed AND purged — removal alone leaves config files behind. Remove it, purge its leftovers, and confirm both the package record and the binary are gone.
symptoms: dpkg -s sl reports the package as installed
Typing 'sl' by accident (instead of 'ls') launches a steam locomotive in the terminal
Security policy requires the purge of config files, not just removal
The audit ticket is not closed until dpkg no longer knows the package
mission: Remove the sl package and purge its configuration files so that `dpkg -s sl` fails and the binary is no longer on the PATH.

hints.title: Check before you change
hints.content: `dpkg -s sl` prints the package record including its status; after a successful purge the same command exits non-zero.

hints.title: remove vs purge
hints.content: `apt-get remove` deletes the program but keeps config files under /etc. `apt-get purge` deletes the program AND its configs.

hints.title: Verify both layers
hints.content: The binary disappearing (`command -v sl`) proves removal; `dpkg -s sl` failing proves the package database is clean too.

acceptance_criteria.description: sl is no longer registered in the package database
the sl binary is gone from the PATH
the dpkg package database is still readable and has installed packages
